title: Grateful Dead Live at The Ark on 1969-04-22

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1969 Boston Ark show highlighted by an epic Dark Star and superb Mountains of the Moon transition.
ai_review.review: The recording, sourced from a 1969 soundboard transfer, is generally clear with a remarkable stereo drum spread, though it suffers from tape hiss, occasional mic feedback and a major cut in The Other One. Musically the night shines – the 30‑minute Dark Star, the seamless Mountains of the Moon segue, tight Eleven and powerful Death Don't Have No Mercy make this one of the era’s standout performances despite some sloppy moments.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen detailed reviews consistently award 4‑5 stars, praising both performance and mix; only isolated technical complaints lower the rating slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp overall sound with excellent stereo placement of Bill & Mickey's drums. Notable tape hiss, early‑set mic feedback and a significant edit/cut in The Other One; Pigpen’s vocal level could be higher.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong opening with Sitting on Top of the World, smooth acoustic‑electric transition into Mountains of the Moon and a marathon Dark Star. The second set maintains momentum despite tape gaps, delivering tight jams and a powerful close.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for raw energy, soaring guitar solos and standout vocals throughout Dark Star and The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for “monster” bass work on The Other One and solid foundation during The Eleven.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ highlighted as prominent and well‑balanced in the mix; overall keyboard work praised.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart receive special commendation for their stereo spread and tight interplay.
